name: Parietal lobe
summary: Behind the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus, bounded behind by the parieto-occipital sulcus. It receives somatic sensation on the postcentral gyrus and integrates it with vision and hearing in the superior and inferior parietal lobules to build a map of the body and of space. The dominant inferior parietal lobule (supramarginal and angular gyri) supports language, calculation, praxis and reading; the non-dominant lobule supports spatial attention. Lesions produce cortical sensory loss, apraxia, neglect, Gerstmann syndrome and inferior quadrantic field defects from the optic radiation passing beneath.

anatomy.location: From the central sulcus to the parieto-occipital sulcus on the lateral and medial surfaces; the intraparietal sulcus separates the superior parietal lobule from the inferior parietal lobule (supramarginal and angular gyri); the precuneus lies on the medial surface.

subdivisions.name: Superior parietal lobule (areas 5, 7)
subdivisions.note: somatosensory association, visuomotor guidance of reaching

subdivisions.name: Angular gyrus (area 39)
subdivisions.note: reading, calculation, finger recognition, semantic integration

subdivisions.name: Precuneus
subdivisions.note: self-referential and visuospatial processing, episodic memory retrieval

function: Somatic sensation and its interpretation, body schema, spatial attention and awareness, visuomotor integration, praxis, and the dominant-side skills of reading, writing and calculation.

bestView.label: superior and inferior parietal lobules behind the postcentral gyrus
precuneus on the medial surface in front of the parieto-occipital sulcus
parietal lobes above the Sylvian fissure

imaging.normalAppearance: Identified behind the central sulcus and in front of the parieto-occipital sulcus on sagittal images; the posterior watershed lies at its junction with the occipital and temporal lobes. Posterior cortical atrophy shows disproportionate parietal and occipital volume loss.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion in the supramarginal and angular gyri and the posterior temporal lobe.
Biparietal and occipital atrophy with Bálint or Gerstmann features and relative hippocampal sparing.
Mass with edema causing cortical sensory loss, apraxia or neglect; a lower quadrantanopia if the radiation is involved.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: DWI and FLAIR; T1 volumetry for atrophy

lesionEffects.deficit: Cortical sensory loss: astereognosis, agraphesthesia, impaired two-point discrimination, extinction
lesionEffects.mechanism: Postcentral gyrus and superior parietal lobule

lesionEffects.deficit: Gerstmann syndrome: acalculia, agraphia, finger agnosia, right-left disorientation (dominant)

lesionEffects.mechanism: Left supramarginal gyrus and its connections
Superior fibers of the optic radiation in the parietal white matter

examination: Stereognosis, graphesthesia, two-point discrimination, double simultaneous stimulation
Line bisection, clock drawing, copying a cube
Pantomime tool use and imitate gestures
pearls: Sensory loss you can only find with a coin in the palm or a number drawn on the skin is cortical (parietal)
The patient who denies a paralyzed left arm has a right parietal lesion
